stem: A 33-year-old day laborer presents with about ten weeks of a firm, gradually enlarging lump in his right groin, which he initially assumed was related to a minor scrape he got on that leg around the same time. It has not been painful most of the time, though it aches after a long day of physical work. He has had occasional low-grade fevers. No prior TB treatment, no known TB contact, no known drug-resistant contact. Fine-needle aspiration of the inguinal node was performed and sent for molecular testing, which was positive for M. tuberculosis. Exam: firm, minimally tender 3 cm right inguinal lymph node, no overlying skin breakdown, no other lymphadenopathy, no genital lesions.

patient.social_history: Lives with roommates; a minor leg scrape occurred around the time the lump was first noticed
patient.presenting_complaint: Firm, gradually enlarging inguinal lump, mild aching after physical work
patient.exam_findings: Firm, minimally tender 3 cm right inguinal lymph node, no overlying skin breakdown, no other lymphadenopathy, no genital lesions
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: A minor scrape on the same leg proposed as the source of a reactive inguinal node, without further workup given the temporal association
A sexually transmitted infection considered given the inguinal location, without examination findings or history supporting it, delaying a targeted aspirate
ntep_correct_actions: Perform upfront molecular testing (NAAT) directly on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen (the inguinal lymph node aspirate) as the first-line microbiological tool, rather than anchoring the workup around culture and histology as the primary reference standard.
who_correct_actions: Perform upfront molecular testing (NAAT) directly on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen (the inguinal lymph node aspirate) as the first-line microbiological tool, rather than anchoring the workup around culture and histology as the primary reference standard.
us_correct_actions: Anchor the diagnostic workup for this extrapulmonary presentation around culture and histology as the reference standard, treating molecular testing as a general, conditional adjunct rather than the upfront first-line tool for extrapulmonary specimens.
critical_error_conditions: Attributing the enlarging inguinal node entirely to a minor scrape without pursuing aspirate sampling and molecular testing
expected_divergence_points: Whether upfront molecular testing on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen is the first-line diagnostic tool or culture/histology remains the anchoring reference standard
